reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: AI listed among emerging global challenges
themes.definition: AI named alongside cybersecurity, terrorism, cybercrime or genetic engineering as a frontier or emerging issue, without further argument about AI itself.
themes.inclusion: Include passages where AI is an item in a list of new challenges the UN or multilateralism must address.
themes.exclusion: Exclude passages that describe specific AI governance tools, programmes or policy positions.
themes.boundary_cases: Mention of 'economic disruption' from AI within such a list stays here unless the passage develops labour or economic effects.

examples.quote: the economic disruption caused by the emergence of digital technologies, including artificial intelligence and the potential for genetic engineering
Frontier issues such as artificial intelligence and cybercrime have leapt from the pages of science fiction into our daily lives.

themes.label: AI as global commons needing common rules
themes.definition: AI treated as a domain of the global commons requiring multilateral cooperation, common rules and trust-building, with rules framed as enabling rather than slowing progress.
themes.inclusion: Include passages calling for multilateral commitment on AI as global commons or arguing that common rules and safeguards enable faster AI progress.
themes.exclusion: Exclude passages only listing AI as a challenge without calling for cooperation or rules.
themes.boundary_cases: Offering national governance frameworks and testing tools to others fits here and in AI_CAPACITY_BUILDING.

examples.quote: We need to bring the same constructive spirit to other areas of the global commons — AI, cybersecurity, digital technology and even outer space.
powerful engines and good brakes and common rules do not stop us or slow us down

themes.label: Small-state AI capacity-building programmes
themes.definition: Singapore offering capacity-building, governance frameworks and testing tools to small states and SIDS on digital technologies and AI.
themes.inclusion: Include passages announcing training programmes, technical assistance, or sharing of AI governance tools with other states.
themes.boundary_cases: Forum of Small States digital pillar activities count here when AI is explicitly or contextually included.

examples.quote: including Leadership and Governance in the Age of Digital Technologies and Artificial Intelligence
making our governance frameworks and testing tools available to all

value.rationale: Singapore passages across years embed AI in a small-state multilateralism narrative: early speeches only list AI among emerging challenges, later ones treat AI as a global commons needing common rules and offer capacity-building and testing tools to small states.
